summary: This document outlines an exercise to build a responsive single-page application that connects to a shared classroom API. The goal is to create a frontend that can list signups and allow users to add their own names via GET and POST requests.
key_facts: Build a responsive single-page app that shows everyone who has signed up and lets you add your own name.
The API is intentionally public with no login, class code, authentication header, or API key.
GET /api/signups returns all signups with the newest name first.
POST /api/signups requires a JSON body with one field: { "name": "Ada Lovelace" }.
The app should show loading, empty, success, and error states.
The app must be ready to deploy to Vercel.

concepts.name: UI State Handling
concepts.definition: Designing distinct loading, empty, success, and error views so every request outcome is visible to the user.
concepts.in_this_source: The brief requires friendly loading, empty, success, and error states, and treating status 409 as 'That name is already signed up.'

concepts.name: Vercel
concepts.definition: A cloud platform for developers to build, deploy, and manage web applications.
concepts.in_this_source: The assignment specifies that the app should be ready to deploy to Vercel.

concepts.name: Public Unauthenticated API
concepts.definition: An endpoint anyone can call without credentials, acceptable only for non-sensitive data.
concepts.in_this_source: The signup API deliberately has no login, class code, or API key, and the brief warns not to reuse the pattern for private or sensitive data.
